summary:
All 8 owned files are ported or confirmed portable, and each one compiles cleanly with the strict recipe from ENV_CLOUD.md. Earlier agents had left no changes in these files, so this pass started from the Linux originals.

- automation_scope.c, player_topology.c, silence_detector.c, transition_preset.c and copyright_policy.c are pure logic (GLib/json-glib/GDateTime only). A check for POSIX, path, time-zone, `long`/`time_t` and Linux wording found nothing to change, so they are unchanged.
- external_access.c: when `ca_file == NULL`, the probe now sets `CURLOPT_SSL_OPTIONS = CURLSSLOPT_NATIVE_CA`, as spec 2.13 asks. MSYS2 libcurl 8.23 is built with OpenSSL (checked with `curl -V`), and its compiled-in CA bundle path does not exist on an installed system. An explicit `ca_file` is still used on its own.
- media_archive.c is fully ported to platform.h per spec 2.7 / 6.1:
  - Folder duplicate and nesting checks use `radios_path_equal` / `radios_path_is_inside`.
  - The folder-ready check uses `radios_fs_stat` (follow) plus `radios_fs_dir_check_access(folder, FALSE)`, replacing `access(R_OK|X_OK)`.
  - The directory walk uses `radios_fs_stat(path, FALSE)`. Hidden or system entries are skipped with `radios_file_info_is_hidden` (dot names are still filtered first). `RADIOS_FILE_TYPE_LINK`, which includes junctions, counts as `skipped_links`.
  - mtime is taken from `RadioSFileInfo.mtime_ns` and converted to µs with floor semantics.
  - The index is loaded through `radios_fs_stat` and saved by `radios_fs_mkdir_with_parents(0700)`, then a private temp file (`radios_fs_open` with `CREAT|EXCL|NOFOLLOW`, 0600), write, `radios_fd_sync`, and an atomic `radios_fs_rename`; the temp file is removed on failure.
  - `hash_file` uses `radios_fs_open(RDONLY|NOFOLLOW|CLOEXEC)` and `radios_fd_stat`.
  - The `_XOPEN_SOURCE`, `<unistd.h>`, `<sys/stat.h>`, `<fcntl.h>` and `<glib/gstdio.h>` includes are gone.
- planner.c: the check that `managed_path` lies inside `<database>.objects` was a raw string-prefix test with `G_DIR_SEPARATOR` and `g_path_is_absolute`. It now uses `radios_path_is_absolute`, `radios_path_normalize` on both sides, `radios_path_is_inside` and `!radios_path_equal` (strictly inside, as before). The media path handed to the loader is the normalized path.

No public API changed. Nothing was linked, tested or run under Wine, as this write-only pass requires.
api: No public contract changed. No headers were modified (media_archive.h, external_access.h and playout.h are untouched). Two internal static helpers were added in media_archive.c: write_replace(path, data, length), which does an atomic private replace, and file_has_writer(path), a deny-write sharing probe. New dependencies are platform.h (radios_fs_stat, radios_fs_open, radios_fd_stat, radios_fd_sync, radios_fs_rename, radios_fs_unlink, radios_fs_mkdir_with_parents, radios_fs_dir_check_access, radios_file_info_is_hidden, radios_path_equal, radios_path_is_inside, radios_path_is_absolute, radios_path_normalize) and the CRT _wsopen_s/_SH_DENYWR from <share.h>/<io.h>. No new link libraries are needed.
verification: Ran 'git diff HEAD --stat' on all 8 owned files first: no earlier changes existed, so the pass started from the Linux originals.

Compiled all 8 files as they were with the strict ENV_CLOUD recipe (MSYS2 GCC 16 under Wine; -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -D_FILE_OFFSET_BITS=64 -D_WIN32_WINNT=0x0A00 -DWINVER=0x0A00 -DUNICODE -D_UNICODE, -c only, output in /opt/radios-port/work/c-core-p2/). automation_scope.c, player_topology.c, silence_detector.c, transition_preset.c, copyright_policy.c, planner.c and external_access.c compiled cleanly; media_archive.c failed (st_mtim, S_ISLNK, O_NOFOLLOW/O_CLOEXEC/O_NONBLOCK, fstat with GStatBuf).
Recompiled after porting: media_archive.c, external_access.c and planner.c compile with zero warnings and errors. Objects are in /opt/radios-port/work/c-core-p2/*.o.
Confirmed the MSYS2 libcurl SSL backend with 'ucrt64-tool curl -V' (libcurl 8.23.0 with OpenSSL 3.6.5), which is the backend CURLSSLOPT_NATIVE_CA is documented for on Windows.

Read tests/test_media_archive.c (already ported by its owner: hidden attribute, junction and file-link fixtures, cache re-hash) and checked that the new code follows its expectations. The test was NOT run.
Not done, as this pass requires: no linking, no tests, no Wine runs, no self-review pass.
industrial_fixes: media_archive.c: duplicate and nested archive folders were compared byte-wise, so 'C:\Müzik' and 'c:/müzik/x' passed validation and the same files could be scanned and imported twice. They now go through radios_path_equal / radios_path_is_inside (ordinal case-insensitive, either separator).

media_archive.c: hidden and system entries ($RECYCLE.BIN, System Volume Information at the root of every USB archive disk) were walked or reported as unreadable on every scan. They are now skipped with radios_file_info_is_hidden after a no-follow stat.

media_archive.c: link detection is now reparse-point based (RADIOS_FILE_TYPE_LINK), so junctions and mount points are counted as skipped_links and never followed. g_lstat/S_ISLNK cannot see links on Windows, so a junction loop or a junction into another archive folder would otherwise have been walked.

media_archive.c: a file still being copied could be hashed and imported with a wrong digest. Explorer/CopyFileEx size the target to its final length first and set the source mtime only at the end, so the size/mtime-unchanged check alone cannot catch it. A deny-write sharing probe after hashing (_wsopen_s with _SH_DENYWR; a sharing violation means a writer handle is still open) now rejects the file with the existing 'okunurken değişti (kopyalama sürüyor olabilir)' message, and it is retried on the next scan. Read-only openers such as FFmpeg/players and AV scanners do not trip it.

media_archive.c: the index cache was written with g_file_set_contents_full. On Windows that ignores 0600 and uses MoveFileExW without retry, so it fails while AV or the Search indexer holds the old index. It now uses a private temp file, FlushFileBuffers, and radios_fs_rename (POSIX-semantics replace with a bounded retry); the temp file is removed on failure and the parent folder is created through radios_fs_mkdir_with_parents(0700).
media_archive.c: the folder-ready check is now ACL-accurate (radios_fs_dir_check_access opens and lists the directory). The old access(R_OK|X_OK) ignores ACLs, and the UCRT rejects X_OK.

media_archive.c: errno is now saved before g_io_error_from_errno/g_strerror in the open and read error paths. The dead EINTR retry (never reported by the UCRT _read) was removed (D2b), and the unused O_NONBLOCK flag (no FIFOs on Windows) was dropped.

external_access.c: the HTTPS reachability probe used libcurl's compiled-in OpenSSL CA bundle path, which points into the MSYS2 build prefix and does not exist on an installed system, so every probe would have failed with a certificate error. Without an explicit ca_file it now trusts the Windows certificate store (CURLSSLOPT_NATIVE_CA).

planner.c: the managed media path check (the file must lie inside '<database>.objects') was a byte prefix test with G_DIR_SEPARATOR plus g_path_is_absolute. On Windows it rejected valid paths that differ only in case or separator (for example tests whose roots use '/', W19), and it accepted rooted '\foo' paths as absolute. It now normalizes both sides ('..' resolved), uses radios_path_is_absolute and radios_path_is_inside, and requires strictly-inside (not equal) as before.
requests_for_other_areas: config.c / data_client.c owners: give RadioSPlayoutRequest.database_file (the config database path) in realpath form (radios_fs_realpath: long names, final case, subst/mapped drives resolved). The planner now compares SDBASE's managed_path against '<database_file>.objects' with Windows path rules. That handles case and separators, but not 8.3 short names: %TEMP% is C:\Users\SONATT~1\... on the user's PC. If C keeps an 8.3 spelling while Python returns a resolved long path, every planned entry would be rejected with 'Medya yönetilen istasyon arşivinin dışında.'

Python/SDBASE port: version.managed_path must be an absolute Windows path (drive or UNC) without a '\\?\' prefix. C rejects device-prefixed paths as not absolute (radios_path_is_absolute). Either separator is accepted.

Platform layer owner (optional): add a 'writer still open' probe to platform.h, for example gboolean radios_fs_has_writer(const gchar *path) using a CreateFileW deny-write share open with the \\?\ long-path rules, or a RADIOS_O_DENY_WRITE open flag. media_archive.c could then drop its local _wsopen_s probe, which builds the \\?\ / \\?\UNC\ prefix itself for paths of 240 or more characters.
open_issues: Nothing was linked, tested or run under Wine (write-only pass). tests/test_media_archive.c, test_external_access.c and the playout/automation tests that exercise planner.c still need to be built and run on the user's PC.

media_archive.c file_has_writer(): it treats only EACCES from _wsopen_s(_SH_DENYWR) as 'writer present'; any other error (for example a long path the CRT cannot open) fails open, and the size/mtime check still applies. On real Windows, verify that a file being copied by Explorer is rejected and hashed on the next scan, and that files open in RadioS's own player (FFmpeg, read-only) are not rejected.

media_archive.c: the index cache keys and the 'seen' table are still case-sensitive path strings, as spec 2.7 states is acceptable (paths come from directory enumeration). A folder re-added with different case only causes a one-time re-hash.

media_archive.c write_replace(): a crash between the temp-file create and the rename leaves a '<index>.xxxxxxxx.tmp' file in the cache folder; GLib had the same behaviour. It is a harmless cache leftover with no cleanup sweep.

planner.c: the containment check is purely lexical (normalize + is_inside). As in the Linux original, it does not resolve links/junctions inside '<database>.objects'; the audio loader's own no-follow open of media files (audio area) is the enforcement point for that.
